headline: High data-leakage and compliance risk: Khoj’s broad networked retrieval can expose indexed personal notes, while awesome-prompts is a docs-only prompt source with no isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt repository and Khoj ingests retrieved content into chat/RAG. If prompt text from agent_a is copied into agent_b’s indexed notes or search corpus, agent_b may treat attacker-controlled instructions as trusted content. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from the profiles and uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF agent_a content is imported into agent_b’s indexed documents or chat context
IF agent_b renders retrieved text as instructions without provenance labeling
mitigations: Keep agent_a content out of agent_b’s indexed corpus
Add a provenance banner to retrieved snippets
Disable automatic instruction-following on retrieved text
Review imported prompt files before indexing
requires-engineering: add source-trust tagging in the retrieval pipeline

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b reads indexed personal notes/files and can use broad network egress to send context to a cloud or configured search provider. agent_a has no filesystem or network surface, so it is not a leak source itself, but pairing it with Khoj creates a path where sensitive notes can be exposed through retrieval and outbound requests. The shared-workspace assumption is not documented, so uncertainty remains.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured with cloud search or remote model providers
IF personal notes or indexed documents contain sensitive data
mitigations: Use self-hosted-only providers for agent_b
Exclude sensitive folders from indexing
Rotate or restrict model API keys
Audit outbound requests for retrieved text
requires-engineering: add per-document redaction before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a is non-runnable and has no write or network capabilities; agent_b cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is read-side content handling, so the pair lacks the mutable-resource collision that would raise severity.
conditions: IF agent_a is manually copied into a shared mutable workspace
IF agent_b is granted additional write or git permissions outside this profile
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not grant agent_b write or git access
Avoid manual copy into shared repos
Document read-only boundaries
requires-engineering: add workspace locking if write access is later enabled

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a prompt-writing source, and agent_b is a retrieval/chat system that can surface indexed content to users. If agent_b treats imported prompt text as authoritative, errors or misleading instructions from agent_a can cascade into downstream answers. There is no documented verification step or provenance filter, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a prompts are imported into agent_b’s knowledge base
IF agent_b answers without source verification or human review
mitigations: Mark imported prompts as untrusted
Require citations for retrieved claims
Add a review step before publishing outputs
Limit agent_b to summarization of imported content
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware retrieval scoring

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents and may use cloud or configured search providers, creating a residency/retention mismatch risk if those notes include regulated data. agent_a is a docs-only prompt repository and is not itself a compliance sink, so the main concern is agent_b’s handling of user data and outbound services.
conditions: IF indexed documents include regulated personal data
IF agent_b is connected to a non-compliant cloud provider or search backend
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b indexes
Use a self-hosted deployment
Review retention settings for connected providers
Restrict API keys to least privilege
requires-engineering: add data-class-based routing and retention controls
